terms.grammar: pronoun and adjective (as a pronoun, neuter quicque); never first in its clause
evidence: Cato Agr. 5.5: utī suō quisque locō cubet
terms.comment: The “each” of more than two; of two, uterque (see both). It leans on the word before it: after sē or suus (suō quisque locō, each in his own place), after a relative or a question word (quot quisque habēret, how many each had), after a superlative or an ordinal (see every). With a superlative, “all the …, every one in his degree”: sapientissimus quisque, all the wisest; neuter optimum quidque, all the best things.

terms.grammar: pronoun and adjective; both parts decline (dat. ūnīcuique); also written apart
evidence: Cato Agr. 58: salis ūnīcuique in annō modium satis est

terms.gloss: each one separately; one to each
evidence: Cato Agr. 148.1: in culleōs singulōs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Each by himself, one apiece; opposed to ūniversī, all together. With a distributive number, so many each: bīnī, two each (see two each).

phrases.latin: prius vīllam videat clausa utī siet, et utī suō quisque locō cubet
phrases.english: first let him see that the farmhouse is locked, and that each man is sleeping in his own place

phrases.latin: haec postquam omnia sēcrēvimus, tum suō quaeque locō disposuimus
phrases.english: when we had sorted all these things, we put each in its own place

phrases.latin: lautī cibum capiunt: sēparātae singulīs sēdēs et sua cuique mēnsa
phrases.english: when they have washed, they eat: each has a seat of his own and his own table

phrases.latin: ut quisque aetāte antecēdit, ita sententiae prīncipātum tenet
phrases.english: each speaks first as he is first in age

phrases.latin: salis ūnīcuique in annō modium satis est
phrases.english: a peck of salt a year is enough for each man

phrases.latin: sapientissimus quisque aequissimō animō moritur, stultissimus inīquissimō
phrases.english: the wisest die with the calmest mind, the most foolish with the least calm

phrases.latin: in omnī enim arte vel studiō vel quāvīs scientiā vel in ipsā virtūte optimum quidque rārissimum est
phrases.english: for in every art or study or any knowledge, or in virtue itself, the best is always the rarest
